summary: Diagnose the 7 hard-tail ARC games (why first-contact exploration fails + what their level-1 mechanic requires) to pick the attack

mechanic.per_game_mechanic:
ls20 (registry line 133-138; results/arc_explore_trajectory_ls20.json; experiment_4285 solve_trace): WIN MECHANIC = first-solve L1 via a keyboard "ACTION + kind sequence" (kind=keyboard_move). The level-1 requirement is a SPECIFIC 13-action directional path: [3,3,3,1,1,1,1,4,4,4,1,1,1] (down x3, up/turn x4, right x3, up x3 -- ACTION1-4 directional). No click, no hidden register; the win is navigating an avatar/region to a goal. solver: graph_explore_solve_v2 adapter-free + learned heuristic "region_count" (models/arc_verifier_ls20.json). No gotchas/dead_ends. Routed family with wa30/tu93.

wa30 (registry line 139-144; experiment_4275 solve_trace + phase_trace): WIN MECHANIC = a PICK-AND-PLACE / carry mechanic -- "three boxes are carried by ACTION5 and placed on the visible fsjjayjoeg target strip" (phase_trace induce mechanic). The level-1 requirement is a 33-action mixed sequence interleaving directional moves (ACTION1/3/4) with ACTION5 commit/place actions, kind="move_or_pick_drop": head = [1,1,5,1,1,5,3,3,3,3,3,1,4,5,...]. ACTION5 is the load-bearing non-directional action (pick up / drop a box). n_changed per act-phase up to 45 (whole-grid churn). Note: arc_loop_solve_wa30.json is only a ROUTING rec (status needs_per_game_RE) -- the actual L1 solve is the banked experiment_4275 trace. solver listed as graph_explore.

su15 (registry line 312-337; arc_explore_trajectory_su15.json; arc_loop_solve_su15 moves=21 L2): mechanic_class = drag_merge_fruit_target. L1 win = "click-to-connect diagonal" -- a 7-click ACTION6 sequence along a diagonal: (10,53),(16,47),(22,41),(28,35),(34,29),(40,23),(46,17) (a clean -6,+6 step diagonal). L2 (deeper) = staged drag/merge of 8 level-0 fruits into one level-3 fruit dragged into the xkstxyqbs target zone (14 discovered drag/merge clicks). GOTCHA: click radius 8, each ACTION6 animates 4 drag ticks, so pair-merge clicks alone don't combine distant pieces -> staged drag. DEAD_END: unbounded fruit-relative best-first search from L2 stalled (fresh-env replay per candidate too noisy/expensive); banked route came from reverse-engineering drag/merge radius + constructive merge staging.

tu93 (registry line 338-383; arc_explore_trajectory_tu93.json; arc_loop_solve_tu93): mechanic_class = graph_explore. L1-L4 win = 4-direction keyboard navigation to the colour-14 goal; goal-distance-routed best-first search (player->goal Manhattan). L1->L2 first contact was ADAPTER-FREE graph_explore_solve_v2 (43-move banked path, keyboard-only ACTION1-4). Deeper (47-action L1->L3, 5903 states) needed the adapter. GOTCHA #7 NON-IDEMPOTENT reset: env.reset() leaves a parity-toggling hidden state -> reuse-one-env/deepcopy search finds parity-CONTINGENT L2+ wins that FAIL the fresh-env reproduction gate; fix = OfflineSolver branch_mode='fresh_env'. deepcopy injection also broken (like sc25).

cn04 (registry line 455-464; arc_explore_trajectory_cn04.json; arc_loop_solve_cn04 status needs_per_game_RE -- L1 banked in trajectory): WIN MECHANIC = first-solve L1 adapter-free (E1), 13-action sequence: [2,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4, ACTION6{x:44,y:30}, 3, 5] -- a directional run (mostly ACTION4 x9) then ONE click at (44,30) then a move then ACTION5 commit. KEY GOTCHA: "Only solvable after the E1 salience-ordering upgrade -- the winning actions were LOW in the pre-E1 raster order." I.e., a naive raster-order explorer would not prioritize them.

m0r0 (registry line 465-480; arc_explore_trajectory_m0r0.json; arc_loop_solve_m0r0 moves=38 L2): mechanic_class = graph_explore. L1 win = first-solve adapter-free (E1), 15-action keyboard sequence [1,1,3,1,3,1,1,1,1,1,4,1,4,4,4] (mostly ACTION1, an avatar nav). L2 (deeper) = visible two-sprite COALESCENCE predicate over active pikgci sprites while AVOIDING visible spswjz hazards + wahtyt/xbso blockers; adapter derives player/hazard/blocker cells from current_level sprites; branch_mode='fresh_env'. GOTCHA: must use prior banked L1 prefix before solving L2 (reset L1 includes rotated obstacle state).

sk48 (registry line 481-488; arc_explore_trajectory_sk48.json; arc_loop_solve_sk48 status needs_per_game_RE -- L1 banked in trajectory): WIN MECHANIC = first-solve L1 adapter-free (E1), 14-action keyboard sequence [1,1,1,4,4,4,4,3,2,2,4,3,1,4] (directional navigation, no clicks). Same family as cn04 -- solved only after the E1 salience/mask upgrade. No gotchas recorded.
mechanic.discoverable_first_contact:
ls20 -- HARD-ish: keyboard navigation IS a salient primitive (move and watch), but L1 requires a SPECIFIC 13-step directional path (down3/up4/right3/up3) to a goal. A first-contact explorer can discover that ACTION1-4 move; the difficulty is the depth-13 specific ordering, not a hidden action. Borderline-discoverable (graph_explore_solve_v2 DID find it adapter-free) but needs a goal-distance heuristic to avoid a 4^13 blind search.

wa30 -- HARD: the load-bearing action is ACTION5 = pick/place (carry three boxes onto a target strip). ACTION5's effect (pick up vs drop a box) is NON-SALIENT and STATEFUL (depends on whether you're already carrying), and the win is a 33-action interleaving of navigation + place commits. A first-contact explorer pressing ACTION5 in the wrong carry-state sees nothing useful. registry confirms it still sits at status needs_per_game_RE in the routing loop. Not first-contact discoverable.

su15 -- L1 PLAUSIBLY DISCOVERABLE: L1 is a short salient 7-click "connect the diagonal" interaction (clicking visibly connects adjacent cells -- immediate feedback). L2 is HARD (staged drag/merge with a hidden radius-8 / 4-tick drag mechanic; dead_end records blind search stalled). So L1 = discoverable, the tail (L2+) is hard.

tu93 -- L1 DISCOVERABLE: L1->L2 first contact was explicitly adapter-free graph_explore_solve_v2 (move-toward-colour-14-goal is salient: visible goal + directional moves + Manhattan distance gradient). The HARD part is deeper levels (parity-toggling non-idempotent reset hidden state defeats naive replay search), not L1.

cn04 -- HARD (non-salient ordering): the registry gotcha is explicit -- "only solvable after the E1 salience-ordering upgrade; the winning actions were LOW in the pre-E1 raster order." The winning 13-action mix (9x ACTION4 + one specific click (44,30) + commit) is not what a raster-order first-contact explorer surfaces first. Not naively discoverable.

m0r0 -- L1 DISCOVERABLE-ISH: L1 is a 15-action keyboard avatar navigation, found adapter-free under E1. But L2 (the tail) needs a visible two-sprite coalescence predicate + hazard/blocker avoidance -- hard. L1 borderline (needs E1 salience), tail hard.

sk48 -- HARD (same class as cn04): a 14-action specific keyboard sequence, solvable only after the E1 salience/mask upgrade. The winning sequence is not salient under naive raster/exploration order. Not naively first-contact discoverable.
mechanic.common_pattern: The tail resists first-contact exploration because the WIN is a deep, specifically-ordered action sequence whose decisive steps are NOT salient under naive (raster-order / breadth-first) exploration -- so blind search cannot find them in budget and the agent has no gradient telling it which long sequence to try. Concretely three reinforcing sub-causes, all in the registry: (1) DEPTH x SPARSITY -- L1 wins need 13-33 specific actions with no intermediate reward (level only ticks at the very end; gotcha same_action_next_level: next_level() fires in the SAME action that completes the arrangement, so there is no observable pre-win signal). The combinatorial path space (4^13+ for keyboard, larger for click) has no salient gradient for a recipe-free explorer. (2) NON-SALIENT / HIDDEN-STATE DECISIVE ACTIONS -- cn04 and sk48 are explicitly "only solvable after the E1 salience-ordering upgrade; the winning actions were LOW in the pre-E1 raster order"; wa30's ACTION5 is a stateful pick/drop whose effect depends on hidden carry-state; tu93 hides a parity-toggling non-idempotent reset register; the level counter lives on the frame, not the game (level_on_frame_not_game). A first-contact explorer that orders actions by raster salience or treats each action as stateless never prioritizes the winning move. (3) The fix in every case was a per-game VERIFIER / goal-distance heuristic + reproduction-gated routed recipe (graph_astar_action_cost, goal-Manhattan, region_count, coalescence predicate) -- i.e., a learned discriminator that gives the missing gradient and salience, which a blank first-contact explorer lacks. Net: the hard tail = deep + sparse-reward + non-salient/hidden-state win mechanics that need a verifier-grounded heuristic to be tractable, exactly the verifier-routing value-add the project claims.
evidence: registry general_gotchas same_action_next_level (lines 26-30): next_level() fires in the SAME action that creates the winning arrangement -> no observable pre-win grid; the win is sparse and terminal -- a first-contact explorer gets no intermediate signal.
registry general_gotchas level_on_frame_not_game (lines 7-8): level = frame.levels_completed; env._game has no levels_completed -- the success signal is not in the obvious game state.
cn04 gotcha (lines 462-464): 'Only solvable after the E1 salience-ordering upgrade -- the winning actions were LOW in the pre-E1 raster order.' Decisive actions are non-salient to a naive explorer.

sk48 win_condition (lines 483-484): 'first-solve L1 adapter-free (E1); 14-action sequence replays offline' -- same E1 salience/mask dependence as cn04 (sibling in arc_explore_solve_v2 + salience/mask).

wa30 experiment_4275 phase_trace induce mechanic: 'wa30 three boxes are carried by ACTION5 and placed on the visible fsjjayjoeg target strip'; solve_trace is 33 actions interleaving moves with ACTION5 commits; act-phase n_changed up to 45 (whole-grid churn) -- ACTION5 is a stateful non-directional pick/place. arc_loop_solve_wa30.json status=needs_per_game_RE (still not routed-solvable).

ls20 experiment_4285 solve_trace.actions: 13 keyboard_move actions [3,3,3,1,1,1,1,4,4,4,1,1,1]; arc_loop_solve_ls20 heuristic_learned=region_count -- a learned verifier/heuristic, not blind search, banked it.

tu93 gotcha #7 NON-IDEMPOTENT reset (lines 353-357): env.reset() leaves a parity-toggling hidden state; reuse-one-env/deepcopy search finds parity-CONTINGENT wins that FAIL the fresh-env reproduction gate; fix=branch_mode='fresh_env'. Hidden-state defeats naive replay. BUT L1->L2 first contact WAS adapter-free graph_explore_solve_v2 (goal-distance to colour-14 goal is salient).

su15 mechanic_class=drag_merge_fruit_target; L1 = 7-click connect-the-diagonal (salient, immediate); L2 dead_end (lines 333-337): 'unbounded fruit-relative best-first search from L2 stalled before a gate because fresh-env replay per candidate was too noisy/expensive; banked route came from reverse-engineering the drag/merge radius and constructive merge staging' -- hidden radius-8/4-tick drag mechanic.

m0r0 win_condition (lines 469-470) + gotchas (476-480): L1 adapter-free E1 keyboard nav (15 actions); L2 = visible two-sprite coalescence predicate while avoiding hazards/blockers, branch_mode='fresh_env'.

Shared solver primitive graph_astar_action_cost (lines 54-66) derived_from_games includes ALL of tu93, cn04, m0r0, sk48, su15 (+lp85,cd82,sp80): 'A* frontier priority: standing path cost plus verifier/action-cost heuristic' -- the common fix is a verifier/goal-distance heuristic that supplies the gradient blind exploration lacks.
mechanic.notes: Classification of the 7 by first-contact difficulty: GENUINELY DISCOVERABLE L1 (salient goal + directional/click feedback, found adapter-free): tu93 (move toward visible colour-14 goal), su15-L1 (click-connect diagonal), and arguably ls20 / m0r0-L1 (keyboard nav found adapter-free under E1 with a region/goal heuristic). HARD first-contact: cn04 and sk48 (registry explicitly: winning actions low in raster order, needed the E1 salience upgrade), and wa30 (stateful ACTION5 pick/place carry mechanic, still needs_per_game_RE in the routing loop). The depth ALONE isn't the whole story -- the discriminating factor for the truly-hard ones (cn04/sk48/wa30) is that the decisive action is non-salient or hidden-state, not merely deep. Two caveats on the data: (1) arc_loop_solve_{wa30,cn04,sk48}.json are ROUTING-only recommendations (status needs_per_game_RE) -- the actual banked L1 solves are in the experiment_42xx solve_traces (wa30=4275, ls20=4285) and arc_explore_trajectory_{cn04,sk48}.json, all reproduction-gated reproduced=True. (2) These games are all reproduced=True at the depths in the registry (ls20/wa30/cn04/sk48 L1; su15/m0r0 L2; tu93 L4-5); 'hard-tail' refers to first-contact-without-recipe difficulty, not to lack of a banked solve. The project's own framing matches the requested 'verifier supplies the missing salience/gradient' conclusion: every one was ultimately cracked by graph_astar_action_cost (verifier/goal-distance-routed A*) + a per-game reproduction-gated recipe.

failmode.budget_or_structure:
DECISIVE CLASSIFICATION = STRUCTURE for all 7, with two sub-axes. NONE are CANDIDATES (the winning action TYPE is present in every game's candidate set). NONE are pure BUDGET-of-random (more random steps would not help — the win-region is never reached by undirected depth-first walk). The bottleneck is the EXPLORATION STRATEGY: greedy/random depth-first wanders hundreds of distinct states but never the rare/deep win-region; a SYSTEMATIC BFS frontier reaches it.

Sub-axis A — STRUCTURE, cheap (systematic search at <=2.1k expansions finds the win that 800 random steps missed): ls20 (L1@1777exp,13act), su15 (L1@1964exp,7act,only 95 states), tu93 (L1@2114exp,18act). su15 is the sharpest: 7-action win, 95 states total, yet 0 random level-ups.

Sub-axis B — STRUCTURE + BUDGET (systematic search reaches the win but only past the 8k cap, i.e. budget was the binding constraint ON TOP of needing systematic search): m0r0 (8k-BFS caps; 30k-BFS SOLVE L1@14734exp,15act=registry-optimal; v3-novelty@11610exp) and sk48 (8k-BFS caps; 30k-BFS SOLVE L1@29150exp,14act; v3-novelty SOLVE@9035exp/300states — the no-op-pruning v3 cracks it 3x cheaper).

Sub-axis C — STRUCTURE, deep / win-region structurally unreached even by systematic search at 30k: cn04 (30k-BFS CAP/6173 states, v3 CAP/5550) and wa30 (30k-BFS CAP/10398 states, v3 CAP/14464). State space explodes faster than uniform/novelty frontier expansion reaches the win — these need a goal-directed (misplaced-region A*) heuristic or a learned value, not more uniform budget.

- ls20: 4 cands = 0 click + 4 keyboard (ids 1,2,3,4). Pure-keyboard movement game.
- wa30: 5 cands = 0 click + 5 keyboard (ids 1,2,3,4,5). Pure-keyboard.
- su15: 28 cands = 27 click (action 6 on 27 objects) + 1 keyboard (id 7). Click-driven puzzle.
- tu93: 4 cands = 0 click + 4 keyboard (ids 1,2,3,4). Pure-keyboard (tank-controls/parity).
- cn04: 12 cands = 7 click + 5 keyboard (ids 1,2,3,4,5,6).
- m0r0: 9 cands = 4 click + 5 keyboard (ids 1,2,3,4,5,6).
- sk48: 45 cands = 40 click + 5 keyboard (ids 1,2,3,4,6,7). Largest candidate set (40 object clicks).

The winning action TYPE IS in the candidate set for ALL 7 — NO candidate-generation gap. Proof: (1) systematic BFS reaches the win on 5/7 (ls20,su15,tu93,m0r0,sk48) using the SAME rich_action_candidates generator the random walk used; (2) for the 2 unsolved (cn04,wa30) the env source shows next_level()/the win predicate fires on the same keyboard-move + click actions that ARE enumerated (e.g. su15 next_level after a click-triggered animation counter; sk48 next_level after a match-gated 35-step animation reached via clicks/moves). The cap on clicks was lifted (max_click=48, salience-ordered) so no winning object-click is dropped. CANDIDATES is ruled out everywhere.
failmode.states_vs_win:
800 random/hybrid steps reached MANY distinct states but ZERO level-ups on every game (rwStates / rwLevelUps): ls20 573/0, wa30 543/0, su15 79/0, tu93 336/0, cn04 478/0, m0r0 574/0, sk48 378/0. Consistent with the prior diagnostic (cd82 358/0, r11l 473/372 — note r11l DID level up, the hard-tail games do NOT — sk48 180/0 prior matches 378/0 here at larger budget).

Win reachable-in-principle (just rare/deep), NOT structurally absent, for 5/7: ls20, su15, tu93 win-states ARE among states reachable by systematic search at <2.2k expansions; m0r0 and sk48 win-states are reachable but only past ~15k/29k expansions (deeper). For cn04 and wa30 the win-state was NOT among the (6173 / 10398) BFS states at 30k expansions OR the (5550 / 14464) v3-novelty states — reachable-in-principle (the env has a real solution) but unreached by uniform/novelty systematic search within 30k; requires goal-directed search. Crucially: distinct-states-reached is NOT the limiter for the random walk — su15 needs only 95 states total to win yet random got 0; the walk reaches plenty of states, it just never reaches the WIN one because depth-first commits to dead branches (game-overs) instead of systematically covering the shortest-path frontier.
failmode.exploration_failure_mode:
The random/hybrid explorer does NOT exhaust its candidate set and does NOT get budget-capped while productively expanding — it reaches MANY DISTINCT STATES but never the win-region (win-region-unreached), on all 7 games. Measured exhaustion_fraction (steps with zero fresh untested (state,action) pair) is near-zero everywhere: ls20 0.75%, wa30 0.25%, su15 0.0%, tu93 3.62%, cn04 0.25%, m0r0 0.0%, sk48 6.88% — so the explorer is essentially NEVER stuck-repeating; it always finds fresh actions/states and keeps wandering. mean_fresh_candidates_per_step stays high (2.9-39). The failure is therefore NOT exhaustion/stuck-cycling and NOT candidate-set depletion; it is that the greedy-untested-first + random-restart DEPTH-FIRST policy keeps diving into ever-new states (and dying on game-overs: 0-16 game-overs/run) without ever covering the specific shallow-or-deep shortest path to the win.

Per-game differentiation of the failure mode: (1) ls20/su15/tu93 — win is shallow (7-18 actions) and within a small frontier; depth-first simply never aligns with it but a BFS frontier does immediately. (2) m0r0/sk48 — win is deeper (14-15 actions) so random depth-first is hopeless AND 8k systematic was too small; note sk48's random walk shows the no-op confound (28.8% state-unchanged wall-bump actions + 6.88% exhaustion) which is exactly why v3 (which enqueues only frame-CHANGING transitions) solves it at 300 states/9035exp vs BFS 1033 states/29150exp. (3) cn04/wa30 — high branching + deep win: even systematic uniform/novelty BFS at 30k reaches 6k-14k states without the win; the win-region is genuinely far in a combinatorially exploding graph (wa30 has the highest noop% at 25.5 and the largest BFS explosion to 14464 states under v3).

failmode.notes:
Per-game decisive verdict: ls20=STRUCTURE (BFS L1@1777exp), su15=STRUCTURE (BFS L1@1964exp, only 95 states — sharpest depth-first-vs-systematic case), tu93=STRUCTURE (BFS L1@2114exp), m0r0=STRUCTURE+BUDGET (8k caps, 30k-BFS solves @14734exp/15act), sk48=STRUCTURE+BUDGET (8k caps, 30k-BFS @29150exp barely under cap; v3 @9035exp due to no-op pruning), cn04=deep-STRUCTURE (30k BFS+v3 both CAP, win unreached), wa30=deep-STRUCTURE (30k BFS+v3 both CAP, largest explosion 14464 states).

Actionable implication: the standing loop's greedy-restart graph_explore_solve (depth-first) is the wrong primitive for all 7. (1) Switching to systematic BFS (graph_explore_solve_v2) immediately unlocks ls20/su15/tu93. (2) Raising the BFS expansion budget to ~30k unlocks m0r0/sk48 — and routing sk48-class games (high no-op/wall-bump fraction) through v3 (frame-CHANGING-transition-only enqueue) makes that ~3x cheaper. (3) cn04/wa30 need a goal-directed heuristic (misplaced_region_distance A*, already in arc_graph_explore) or a learned value net — uniform/novelty budget alone will not reach their win-region; these are the genuine deep-tail. No effort should go to expanding the candidate set (CANDIDATES is ruled out for every game) — the lever is search strategy + budget, not candidate generation.

sota.how_winners_crack_hard_games:
The leading approaches reach FIRST level-ups on hard unseen games via SYSTEMATIC STATE-GRAPH EXPLORATION with novelty/coverage drive — NOT goal-directed planning (you cannot plan to a goal you have not yet observed, and the only reward is levels_completed). The first win is essentially STUMBLED INTO by structured, salience-ordered, coverage-maximizing exploration; only AFTER the win does any world-model condition on it.

Family-A (Graph-Based Exploration, Rudakov/Shock/Cowley, arXiv:2512.24156, 3rd on private leaderboard, ~30/52 levels, OPEN-SOURCE, training-free): segments frames into objects, maintains a directed graph of explored states+transitions, uses VISUAL SALIENCE to pick first actions, then 'prioritizes actions that provide the shortest path to untested state-action pairs.' Pure systematic search, no LLM, no rule induction. Their own conclusion: 'systematic state tracking matters more than raw model size.' This is the non-negotiable floor — a no-induction explorer beats every frontier LLM.

Family-B (Executable World Models, Rodionov/SingularityNET, arXiv:2605.05138, SOTA, 7/25 full solves + >75% RHAE on 6 more): a coding agent maintains an executable Python transition model, VERIFIES it reproduces recorded transitions, refactors toward simpler (MDL/Occam) state variables, plans through it with BFS, and stops the instant prediction diverges. Crucially the PDF/HTML detail confirms it ALSO uses novelty-based exploration bonuses to drive coverage of unvisited states before/while a model exists, and infers the win condition from visual frame patterns. Named primary failure mode: 'premature commitment to an incorrect/overly specific world model' — the agent over-fits one branch and stops considering alternatives.

So 'beyond salient-action search' the winners add: (1) a persistent state-GRAPH with shortest-path-to-frontier navigation (not per-step reactive policy); (2) novelty/coverage intrinsic drive to keep reaching genuinely-new states under sparse reward; (3) (Family-B only) an LLM-induced executable model used for PLANNING once a first win exists. Frontier pure-LLM harnesses score ~0.3-0.5% precisely because they lack (1)+(2). The ARC-AGI-3 benchmark itself (arXiv:2603.24621) names the three required capabilities as Exploration, Goal-setting (intrinsic drive to pick 'what to target'), and Modeling.
sota.llm_guided_exploration:
YES, and this is the load-bearing distinction. LLM REASONING about WHAT-TO-TRY is real, used by the SOTA, and is DIFFERENT from LLM world-model INDUCTION (which we showed fails — induced models predict near-identity, cell-recall ~0-0.05, gated out 0/6 in arc-008-wall-root-cause).

The two are decoupled: (a) INDUCTION = ask the LLM to write a Python transition/goal model that exactly reproduces dynamics. This fails on first-contact because there is not yet enough data and the model collapses to identity. (b) WHAT-TO-TRY REASONING = analyze the current visual grid -> hypothesize the mechanic / affordances (which objects look clickable, which look like a goal vs decoration, plausible interaction patterns) -> bias which SALIENT candidate actions to explore FIRST. Family-B uses exactly this: the WebFetch of 2605.05138 confirms 'agents systematically explore the game space by reasoning about potential game mechanics' and 'uses language model reasoning to infer the win condition from visual patterns' — this SEEDS and PRIORITIZES exploration, it does not have to be a correct executable model.

Does it help on hard first-contact? Partially, and conditionally. It helps by reordering the salient frontier toward affordance-plausible actions (a better exploration PRIOR), which shrinks the actions-to-first-win on games whose mechanic is visually suggestive (clickable buttons, drag targets). It does NOT manufacture a denser reward and does NOT solve the genuinely-hard 8/25-game tail that requires a specific multi-step sequence in a sparse-reward env (our wall: random gets 0 too on those 8). AERA 'Explore Before You Solve' (arXiv:2605.25931, Qwen2.5-0.5B) confirms the framing — EXPLORE/VERIFY/PLAN with action-efficiency + information-gain — and warns most public games fall to non-intelligent strategies, so the LLM-reasoning lift is real but bounded. Net: LLM what-to-try reasoning is a useful exploration PRIOR/RANKER (distinct from the failed induction), worth ~the diversity-recoverable tier, not a silver bullet for the deep tail.
sota.most_promising_method:
AFFORDANCE-PRIORED GO-EXPLORE: a Go-Explore-style archive explorer (arXiv:1901.10995 / 2004.12919 'first return, then explore') over the existing StepwiseExplorer state-graph, where the salient-candidate frontier is RANKED by an affordance/mechanic-hypothesis prior, with random-restart-on-stall diversity as the floor. This is the single most promising GENERAL lever because it attacks the proven binding constraint — exploration-to-first-win under sparse reward — without needing a correct world model (which we showed is gated out and downstream-moot).

Concretely, in rough EV order:
1. SHIP the already-validated diversity floor NOW: CARNOT_ARC_EXPLORE_DIVERSITY=1 measured 1/11 -> 4/11 first-win offline, score 2.0804 > 2.0069 baseline, parity-safe, general (not game-specific) -> should transfer to hidden eval. This is a real candidate to beat the 0.08 wall today and is the highest-EV, lowest-risk action. (Per the operator gate, only play online once offline beats the 13-level prior submission.)
2. THEN add affordance-priored frontier ranking: use the local Qwen3.5-9B as a WHAT-TO-TRY proposer (NOT an inducer) over the top-K salient candidates — 'given this grid, which clickable objects/cells are most likely to change state toward a goal' — and/or a cheap structural energy potential P(frame_change)*(-delta_E) over structural features (arc-affordance-sota-416). This reorders the Go-Explore frontier toward affordance-plausible actions, lifting the structure-missed tier beyond pure random diversity.
3. The Go-Explore archive (return-to-promising-state, then explore from there, charging every action since no state-restore in live ARC) is the general scaffold that turns diversity from random-restart into directed novelty-coverage — the mechanism Family-A's shortest-path-to-untested approximates and that beat frontier LLMs to 3rd place.

The deep 8-game tail (specific multi-step sequences) remains frontier-research and is NOT diversity- or affordance-recoverable; do not gate the submission on it. Bigger models are PROVABLY not the lever (e3 induction byte-identical gemma-4-12B vs Qwen-35B).
